findings.title: Plugin request logs lose traceID
findings.body: The previous `logRequest` appended `traceID` from `tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false)` to the request completion log. This change removes that field and the `tracing` import. The new `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` only adds endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID, and uname; it does not add a trace ID. Unless some unchanged middleware already injects traceID as a contextual log attribute, `Plugin Request Completed` entries will no longer contain a trace ID, breaking log-to-trace correlation.

findings.title: LoggerMiddleware now silently depends on ContextualLoggerMiddleware
findings.body: `LoggerMiddleware` no longer includes pluginId, endpoint, uname, dsName, or dsUID in its own log params. It now calls `m.logger.FromContext(ctx)` and expects those fields to already be present in the context. Production middleware ordering in `CreateMiddlewares` inserts `NewContextualLoggerMiddleware` before it, so the production path gets those fields. However `NewLoggerMiddleware` is exported and can be used independently; any caller that builds a middleware stack without the new contextual middleware will get request logs with those fields silently missing. This hidden ordering dependency should be documented, enforced, or avoided by keeping the fields inside `LoggerMiddleware`.

findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext drops the logger whose logs tests inspect
findings.body: `TestLogger.FromContext` returns `NewTestLogger()` instead of returning `f` or a logger that shares `f`'s `Logs` fields. Since `LoggerMiddleware` now logs via `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)`, any test that passes a `*TestLogger` and then asserts on the original logger's `InfoLogs`/`ErrorLogs` will observe zero calls because the actual log is written to a brand-new `TestLogger`. The fake should preserve the same test logger or share its log counters/fields.

findings.title: Adding FromContext to Logger is a source-breaking interface change
findings.body: The exported `log.Logger` interface now requires `FromContext(context.Context) Logger`. Any existing implementation outside this package, including external/enterprise code, will no longer satisfy the interface and will fail to compile until it adds the method. If `pkg/plugins/log` is consumed as an API, this should be introduced as an optional interface or with a compatibility/deprecation path.

findings.title: Exported InstrumentationMiddleware symbols removed without compatibility aliases
findings.body: This renames the exported `InstrumentationMiddleware` type and `NewInstrumentationMiddleware` constructor to `MetricsMiddleware` and `NewMetricsMiddleware`. Because `pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware` is not an `internal` package, downstream importers such as enterprise or external code will fail to compile after upgrading. If the package is public API, keep deprecated alias symbols during the transition or coordinate the breaking change explicitly.
